title: TCS - Time and Work - Efficiency Multiplier
problemStatement: In a TCS assessment test: A is twice as efficient as B. Working together, they can complete a software sprint in 16 days. In how many days can A complete the sprint working alone?
explanation:
Let B's rate = 1 unit/day. Then A's rate = 2 units/day.
Combined rate = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day.
Total sprint work = 16 days * 3 units/day = 48 units.
Time for A alone = 48 / 2 = 24 days.
source: Campus Drive Memory & X Placement Tracker

title: TCS - Profit and Loss - Marked Price and Discount Margin
problemStatement: A retailer partnering with TCS marks an enterprise license 30% above the cost price and allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. What is the net profit percentage?
explanation:
Let Cost Price CP = 100.
Marked Price MP = 100 * 1.30 = 130.
Selling Price SP after 15% discount = 130 * (1 - 0.15) = 130 * 0.85 = 110.5.
Profit = SP - CP = 110.5 - 100 = 10.5%.
source: Campus Drive Memory & X Placement Tracker

title: TCS - Speed Distance Time - Relative Speed and Rendezvous
problemStatement: Two delivery drones from TCS logistics start simultaneously from points P and Q (distance 300 km) towards each other with speeds of 40 km/h and 60 km/h. At what distance from P will they meet?
explanation:
Relative speed = 40 + 60 = 100 km/h.
Time to meet = Distance / Relative Speed = 300 / 100 = 3 hours.
Distance traveled by drone from P in 3 hours = 40 km/h * 3 h = 120 km.
source: Campus Drive Memory & X Placement Tracker

title: TCS - Simple and Compound Interest Growth Difference
problemStatement: A financial investment tied to TCS cloud savings plan yields a difference of Rs. 240 between compound and simple interest at 8% per annum over 2 years. Find the initial capital.

title: TCS - Syllogism - Three Premises Conditional Validity
problemStatement:
In a TCS reasoning assessment:
Statements:
1. All microservices are scalable.
2. Some scalable systems are fault-tolerant.
3. No fault-tolerant system is vulnerable.
Conclusions:
I. Some microservices are fault-tolerant.
II. Some scalable systems are not vulnerable.
options: C) Both I and II follow
explanation:
Microservices and fault-tolerant sets overlap conditionally through scalable systems, so I is possible but not definite.
Since some scalable systems are fault-tolerant, and no fault-tolerant system is vulnerable, those specific systems are guaranteed not vulnerable. Thus, Conclusion II is strictly valid.
source: Campus Drive Memory & X Placement Tracker

title: TCS - Blood Relations - Coded Family Network
problemStatement:
In a logical test for TCS:
"A @ B" means A is the daughter of B.
"A # B" means A is the husband of B.
"A $ B" means A is the brother of B.
Which expression indicates that "P is the maternal uncle of S"?
explanation:
In option A: "P $ Q" means P is brother of Q.
"Q @ R" means Q is daughter of R.
"R # S" gives the parent connection.
Since P is brother of Q and Q is mother of S, P is the maternal uncle of S.
source: Campus Drive Memory & X Placement Tracker

title: TCS - Circular Seating Arrangement - Center Facing Order

explanation: Arranging in circular order clockwise starting at W: W (pos 1), Y (pos 2), U (pos 3, second to right of W), V (pos 4, adjacent to U), Z (pos 5), X (pos 6, opposite Z). The person immediate right of W (anticlockwise facing center) is Y.

title: Salesforce - Time and Work - Efficiency Multiplier
problemStatement: In a Salesforce assessment test: A is twice as efficient as B. Working together, they can complete a software sprint in 16 days. In how many days can A complete the sprint working alone?
explanation:
Let B's rate = 1 unit/day. Then A's rate = 2 units/day.
Combined rate = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day.
Total sprint work = 16 days * 3 units/day = 48 units.
Time for A alone = 48 / 2 = 24 days.

title: Salesforce - Profit and Loss - Marked Price and Discount Margin
problemStatement: A retailer partnering with Salesforce marks an enterprise license 30% above the cost price and allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. What is the net profit percentage?
explanation:
Let Cost Price CP = 100.
Marked Price MP = 100 * 1.30 = 130.
Selling Price SP after 15% discount = 130 * (1 - 0.15) = 130 * 0.85 = 110.5.
Profit = SP - CP = 110.5 - 100 = 10.5%.

title: Salesforce - Speed Distance Time - Relative Speed and Rendezvous
problemStatement: Two delivery drones from Salesforce logistics start simultaneously from points P and Q (distance 300 km) towards each other with speeds of 40 km/h and 60 km/h. At what distance from P will they meet?
explanation:
Relative speed = 40 + 60 = 100 km/h.
Time to meet = Distance / Relative Speed = 300 / 100 = 3 hours.
Distance traveled by drone from P in 3 hours = 40 km/h * 3 h = 120 km.
